questions.question: By 1914 the Scramble for Africa had left almost the entire continent under European control. Two states stayed independent. How did Ethiopia manage it?
options: Its highlands were considered too poor to be worth taking
The Ottoman Empire guaranteed its borders by treaty
It destroyed an invading Italian army at Adwa in 1896
It signed a protection treaty with Britain and France
questions.answer: It destroyed an invading Italian army at Adwa in 1896
questions.explanation: Menelik II had spent years importing modern rifles and artillery from several European suppliers who were each happy to undercut the others. At Adwa his forces destroyed an Italian army of around 17,000, one of very few decisive African victories over a European power. Italy recognised Ethiopian independence. Liberia, the other survivor, stayed nominally free through American patronage. Adwa became a reference point for anti-colonial movements worldwide.
questions.memory_hook: Menelik II bought modern rifles and artillery from rival European suppliers happy to undercut each other, then destroyed an Italian army of 17,000 at Adwa in 1896. Italy had to recognise Ethiopian independence. Liberia survived through American patronage instead. Adwa became a symbol for anti-colonial movements everywhere.

questions.question: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in April 1961, beating the United States into space. What did he not do on that flight?
options: Communicate with ground control at any point
Complete a full orbit, since he only reached suborbit
Travel alone, since a second cosmonaut flew with him
Land inside his capsule, since he ejected and parachuted
questions.answer: Land inside his capsule, since he ejected and parachuted
questions.explanation: The Vostok capsule had no way to land softly with a person inside, so Gagarin ejected at about 7km and came down under his own parachute. The Soviets concealed this for years because the rules for an official aviation record required the pilot to land with the craft. He did complete a full orbit in 108 minutes. He never flew in space again, since the USSR judged him too valuable to risk, and died in a jet training crash in 1968.
questions.memory_hook: Vostok could not land softly with someone inside, so Gagarin ejected at 7km and parachuted down separately. The USSR hid it because record rules said you had to land with your craft. One full orbit, 108 minutes. He never flew again, deemed too valuable, and died in a jet crash in 1968.

questions.question: The Hundred Years War finally ended in 1453, the same year as another major historical event. What was it?
options: Gutenberg's printing press
The Black Death
Columbus reaching America
The fall of Constantinople
questions.explanation: 1453 was remarkable for two world-changing events: the end of the Hundred Years War and the fall of Constantinople to the Ottoman Turks (May 29, 1453). The fall of Constantinople ended the Byzantine Empire (Eastern Roman Empire) and shifted the balance of power in Europe and the Middle East. Many historians consider it the symbolic end of the Middle Ages.
questions.memory_hook: 1453 = Hundred Years War ends AND Constantinople falls to the Ottomans. Two world-changing events in one year. The end of medieval Europe happens twice simultaneously. The Byzantine Empire had kept Roman civilization alive for 1,000 years — gone in 1453.

questions.question: Figure skating jumps are scored partly by difficulty. What separates the toe jumps from the edge jumps?
options: Toe jumps launch by stabbing the free skate's pick in
Toe jumps must land on the same foot they left from
Toe jumps are performed only in pairs competition
Toe jumps rotate clockwise and edge jumps counter
questions.answer: Toe jumps launch by stabbing the free skate's pick in
questions.explanation: The toe loop, flip and lutz are vaulted off the toe pick of the free foot, while the salchow, loop and axel launch off the skating edge alone. Edge jumps are generally considered harder for the same rotation count because there is no assist. The axel is the only jump entered facing forward, so a triple axel is really three and a half rotations. Toe picks are also why hockey skates cannot be used for figure skating.
questions.memory_hook: Toe jumps, the loop, flip and lutz, vault off the toe pick. Edge jumps, salchow, loop and axel, launch off the blade edge with no assist, so they are harder for the same rotations. The axel takes off facing forward, which is why a triple axel is actually three and a half turns.

questions.question: Kilimanjaro rises 5,895m from the plains of northern Tanzania. What is unusual about climbing it?
options: The summit can only be reached during two months a year
You pass through five climate zones from farmland to ice
It requires technical ice climbing on the final ascent
Climbers must be roped together for the entire route
questions.answer: You pass through five climate zones from farmland to ice
questions.explanation: The trek moves from cultivated farmland through rainforest, heath and moorland, alpine desert, and finally arctic conditions at the summit, the equivalent of walking from the equator to the poles in under a week. No technical climbing is needed on the standard routes, which is why so many attempt it, and why altitude sickness is the real danger. Its glaciers have lost more than 80% of their extent since 1912.
questions.memory_hook: You walk from farmland through rainforest, moorland, alpine desert and into arctic conditions at the top, like crossing from the equator to the poles in a week. No ropes or ice tools on the normal routes, which is exactly why altitude sickness catches people out. The glaciers are more than 80% gone since 1912.

questions.question: A bowling frame can score more than the ten pins standing. How is that possible?
options: A strike adds the next two balls to that frame's score
The tenth frame counts triple for every player
Knocking down all ten on the second ball doubles it
Bonus pins are awarded for consecutive gutter balls
questions.answer: A strike adds the next two balls to that frame's score
questions.explanation: A strike scores ten plus whatever the next two balls knock down, so a frame can reach thirty if the two that follow are also strikes. A spare scores ten plus the next single ball. This is why a perfect game is 300 rather than 120: twelve strikes, each carrying two more forward. It also means your score is not final until later frames are bowled, which is unusual among scoring systems.
questions.memory_hook: A strike is ten plus your next two balls, so a frame can reach thirty. A spare is ten plus the next one ball. That carry-forward is why a perfect game is 300 and not 120, and why your score for a frame is not settled until you have bowled the next ones.

questions.question: James Brown was billed as the hardest working man in show business. What did his band say made the job so demanding?
options: He changed the setlist only minutes before curtain
He refused to rehearse, so every show was improvised
He fined them on stage for missed notes and scuffed shoes
He insisted the band travel separately and unpaid
questions.answer: He fined them on stage for missed notes and scuffed shoes
questions.explanation: Brown ran the band on a fine system, signalling penalties with hand gestures mid-performance for a wrong note, a missed cue, or unpolished shoes. It produced extraordinary tightness and constant turnover, including a famous walkout in 1970 that led him to hire the young musicians who became the JBs, with Bootsy Collins on bass. That rhythmic precision, emphasis hammered onto the first beat, is the foundation of funk and later of hip-hop sampling.
questions.memory_hook: Brown fined his band mid-song with hand signals for wrong notes, missed cues, even scuffed shoes. It made them terrifyingly tight and caused constant walkouts, including one in 1970 that got him Bootsy Collins. That precision, everything slammed onto the one, is where funk comes from.

questions.question: Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) was Marvel's riskiest film to that point. Why did the studio consider it a gamble?
options: Almost nobody had heard of the comic it came from
It had no connection to any other film in the series
It was the first Marvel film shot entirely outside the US
Marvel had lost money on its two previous releases
questions.answer: Almost nobody had heard of the comic it came from
questions.explanation: Marvel had built its run on characters with wide recognition. The Guardians were an obscure title with low sales, fronted by a talking raccoon and a tree with a one-line vocabulary, directed by James Gunn who was known mainly for low-budget horror comedy. It grossed over $770 million. The success shifted studio thinking toward the idea that execution and tone mattered more than a familiar name.
questions.memory_hook: Marvel had always used recognisable characters. This was an obscure comic with poor sales, a talking raccoon, a tree with one line, and a director known for low-budget horror comedy. It made over $770 million and convinced studios that tone and execution beat name recognition.

questions.question: Bohemian Rhapsody, the song, broke the rules of what radio would play in 1975. What made it so unlikely?
options: It was released with no vocals on the first pressing
Nearly six minutes long, with an operatic section in the middle
The band refused to let any station play it before Christmas
It was recorded in a single unedited take with no overdubs
questions.answer: Nearly six minutes long, with an operatic section in the middle
questions.explanation: Radio convention capped singles around three minutes and EMI wanted it cut. Queen refused, and Kenny Everett played it repeatedly on Capital Radio until demand forced the issue. The operatic passage took roughly three weeks, with the band overdubbing vocals so many times the tape reportedly wore thin enough to see through. It topped the UK chart for nine weeks and again after Freddie Mercury's death in 1991.
questions.memory_hook: Radio wanted three minutes; this was six with an opera section in the middle. EMI asked for cuts, Queen refused, and Kenny Everett just played it over and over until demand won. The operatic part took three weeks of overdubs, wearing the tape nearly transparent. Number one for nine weeks, then again in 1991.

questions.question: The Sahara has not always been desert. What was it like around 6,000 years ago?
options: Shallow sea, part of a Mediterranean that reached further south
Grassland and lakes, with hippos, crocodiles and cattle herders
Dense tropical rainforest connected to the Congo basin
Ice-covered, as glaciers reached down into North Africa
questions.answer: Grassland and lakes, with hippos, crocodiles and cattle herders
questions.explanation: During the African Humid Period the Sahara was savannah dotted with lakes, and rock art at Tassili n'Ajjer in Algeria shows cattle, giraffes and people swimming. Lake Chad was many times its present size. A slow shift in Earth's axial tilt weakened the monsoon and the region dried out over centuries, driving populations toward the Nile, which some archaeologists link to the consolidation of Egyptian civilisation. The cycle recurs roughly every 20,000 years.
questions.memory_hook: Six thousand years ago the Sahara was grassland with lakes, hippos and cattle herders, and there is rock art in Algeria showing people swimming. A shift in Earth's tilt weakened the monsoon and it dried out, pushing people toward the Nile. The cycle repeats roughly every 20,000 years.

questions.question: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction without being consumed. How does it manage that?
options: It raises the temperature of the surrounding mixture
It lowers the energy barrier the reaction must clear
It increases how much product the reaction can yield
It adds extra energy directly into the reacting molecules
questions.answer: It lowers the energy barrier the reaction must clear
questions.explanation: Reactions need an activation energy to get started. A catalyst offers an alternative pathway with a lower barrier, so far more molecular collisions have enough energy to react. It does not change how much product you end up with, only how fast you get there, and it emerges unchanged. Enzymes are biological catalysts and can accelerate reactions by factors of millions. Catalytic converters use platinum and palladium the same way.
questions.memory_hook: Reactions need a minimum energy to start. A catalyst opens a lower-energy route, so many more collisions clear the bar. It changes the speed, not the amount of product, and comes out unchanged. Enzymes do this biologically and can speed things up millions of times over.

questions.question: Enzymes speed up reactions in the body, but stop working if things get too hot. Why does heat break them?
options: It strips their electrons, leaving them charged
It unfolds the shape their active site depends on
It makes them react so fast they are used up
It burns them into ash the body cannot rebuild
questions.answer: It unfolds the shape their active site depends on
questions.explanation: An enzyme works because its active site physically fits the molecule it acts on. Heat shakes apart the weak bonds holding that folded shape, and once the shape is lost the fit is gone. This is denaturing, and it is usually irreversible, which is why frying an egg cannot be undone. Human enzymes are tuned to around 37C, which is part of why a high fever is dangerous rather than merely uncomfortable.
questions.memory_hook: An enzyme works by shape: its active site fits the target molecule. Heat shakes apart the weak bonds holding that fold, and the fit is gone. That is denaturing, and it usually cannot be reversed, which is why you cannot unfry an egg. Ours are tuned to 37C, which is why high fever is genuinely dangerous.
